chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: The Decca "Where is the melody" sign and Chick Webb's drums
summary: Decca's studio was cramped, with a sign asking for the melody that was covered whenever Webb's band recorded.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Decca was a good studio, but they didn't have the space -- something they didn't have. They were going into this big band thing -- I know we were crowded in there when we did Chick Webb. We came off the road, the band was blowing like mad, you know, and they had to, "Hey, take it easy," you know. Chops was up (inaudible), you know. The brass was -- half of them guys were pumping, you know. And they had a thing there. They had a Mona Lisa -- a statue of a woman, you know, and had this thing -- As you walk in, you see this, you look up -- (inaudible) there's a door up there. And they had written down in there, "Where is the melody," you know, "Where is the melody." The bands would come in and they would play. These guys be playing, be jamming. The guy says, "Where's the melody? Where's the melody to this thing? What's the name of it?" You know. And so, they had -- this is the truth --

this is the honest to God truth. I ain't just making this up. This is a truestory. Like all the stuff I'm telling you (inaudible), this is really true.

When we went in to record, they used to put a white sheet over it to cover this thing up. He says, "Why yall do that, Chick? Why you do that?" He says, "Well the man that plays a beautiful melody is here today." [Chuckles] (inaudible) Chick Webb's band is here. They play beautiful." Had to cover it up. They had a big sign, this (inaudible) Mona Li -- "Where's the melody." Written in big letters, you know. And when Chick Webb came in to play, (inaudible) they covered it up. And that really happened. And I say, "Why yall cover the sign?" He say, "Well, the melody is here today." I say, "Oh, come on." Yeah, you know. But we always had trouble in recording because they didn't know where to put the drums. And Chick was so heavy and powerful, they had to put him in the door cage over there (inaudible). Finally found a spot (inaudible).
